Symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery pustules in stripes along leaf veins; leaves dry early
Relevant_Conditions: Cool (10-15 C), humid weather with dew in Jan-Feb; susceptible varieties
Recommended_Action: Spray a recommended triazole fungicide (e.g. propiconazole or tebuconazole) at first appearance; repeat after 15-20 days if spread continues
Prevention: Sow rust-resistant approved varieties; avoid excess nitrogen; sow at recommended time (Nov 1-20)
Applicable_District_Region: Wheat areas, mainly northern & central Punjab: Sialkot, Gujranwala, Narowal, Gujrat, Rawalpindi, Attock
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans; CIMMYT Wheat & Maize Doctor

Symptoms: Round orange-brown pustules scattered on leaf surface; leaves turn yellow then dry
Relevant_Conditions: Moderate temperature (15-25 C) with humidity during Feb-March; late sowing
Recommended_Action: Apply recommended triazole fungicide when infection reaches 5-10% of flag leaf area
Prevention: Grow resistant varieties; timely sowing; balanced fertilizer
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans; CIMMYT Wheat & Maize Doctor

Symptoms: Elongated dark red-brown pustules on stems and leaf sheaths; stems weaken and lodge
Relevant_Conditions: Warm (20-30 C) humid weather late in season; late-sown crop
Recommended_Action: Spray triazole fungicide immediately; harvest promptly at maturity
Prevention: Use resistant varieties (Ug99-resistant lines); avoid late sowing
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: CIMMYT Wheat & Maize Doctor; Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC)

Symptoms: Whole ear converted to black powdery mass of spores at heading
Relevant_Conditions: Infected seed from previous crop
Recommended_Action: Rogue out and destroy smutted heads before spores spread
Prevention: Treat seed with systemic fungicide (carboxin+thiram or tebuconazole) before sowing; use certified seed
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans

Symptoms: Grains partly black and powdery with fishy smell at tip (embryo end)
Relevant_Conditions: Rain and high humidity at heading (Feb-March)
Recommended_Action: No curative action; separate infected grain lots from seed use
Prevention: Use certified disease-free seed; avoid irrigation during heading in humid weather; crop rotation
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC); CABI Plantwise Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: White to grey powdery growth on leaves and sheaths, later with black dots
Relevant_Conditions: Cool, cloudy, humid weather; dense crop with high nitrogen
Recommended_Action: Spray sulphur-based or triazole fungicide if more than 10% leaf area affected
Prevention: Balanced N application; optimum seed rate; resistant varieties
Applicable_District_Region: Northern Punjab: Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum, Chakwal, Sialkot
Source: CIMMYT Wheat & Maize Doctor

Symptoms: Clusters of small green/black insects on ears and leaves; sticky honeydew; shrivelled grain
Relevant_Conditions: Mild, dry, cloudy weather Feb-March; excess nitrogen
Recommended_Action: Spray recommended insecticide only if more than 10-15 aphids per tiller; prefer selective chemistry to protect ladybird beetles
Prevention: Timely sowing; avoid excess nitrogen; conserve natural enemies
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories; Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans

Symptoms: Seedlings cut at base, patches of dead plants; termite tunnels in soil
Relevant_Conditions: Sandy and rain-fed soils, dry conditions
Recommended_Action: Apply recommended soil insecticide with irrigation water
Prevention: Seed treatment with recommended insecticide; use well-decomposed manure
Applicable_District_Region: Thal & rain-fed (barani): Bhakkar, Layyah, Khushab, Mianwali, Jhang, Chakwal, Attock
Source: Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories

Symptoms: Grassy weeds resembling wheat seedlings competing heavily; reduced tillers
Possible_Cause: Wild oat (Avena fatua) and Phalaris minor (dumbi sitti)
Relevant_Conditions: Rice-wheat system, repeated wheat cropping, zero tillage
Recommended_Action: Apply recommended post-emergence grass herbicide 30-40 days after sowing on moist soil
Prevention: Crop rotation; rotate herbicide groups to avoid resistance; use clean seed; stale seedbed
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat; central Punjab
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans; CIMMYT Wheat & Maize Doctor

Symptoms: Broad-leaf weeds (bathu, maina, jangli palak) covering crop rows
Relevant_Conditions: Cotton-wheat zone, high soil moisture
Recommended_Action: Apply recommended broad-leaf herbicide 25-35 days after sowing
Prevention: Hand weeding / hoeing; certified seed; timely first irrigation
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans

Symptoms: Older leaves turn pale yellow from tip, plants stunted, few tillers
Relevant_Conditions: Low organic matter soils; delayed or skipped top-dressing; sandy soils
Recommended_Action: Top-dress urea in split doses with first and second irrigation
Prevention: Soil testing; apply N in 2-3 splits; include legumes or manure in rotation
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept); Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans

Symptoms: Dark green to purplish leaves, poor root growth and tillering
Relevant_Conditions: Calcareous alkaline soils (pH > 8) common across Punjab fix phosphorus
Recommended_Action: Apply DAP/SSP at sowing; foliar P can help temporarily
Prevention: Band-place P at sowing based on soil test; add organic matter
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept)

Symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on middle leaves, stunted plants
Relevant_Conditions: Calcareous, high-pH soils, high P application, rice-wheat system
Recommended_Action: Foliar spray of zinc sulphate (0.5%)
Prevention: Apply zinc sulphate to soil at sowing every 2-3 years on deficient soils
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat; central Punjab
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept)

Symptoms: Premature drying of leaves, shrivelled light grains, early maturity
Relevant_Conditions: Temperatures above 32-34 C in late March-April; late sowing
Recommended_Action: Light irrigation at grain filling to cool canopy (avoid in windy weather to prevent lodging)
Prevention: Sow on time (Nov 1-20); heat-tolerant varieties
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah; southern Punjab
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans; Pakistan Meteorological Department - agromet advisories

Symptoms: Crop wilting, rolled leaves, poor tillering and small ears
Relevant_Conditions: Rain-fed areas with below-normal winter rainfall
Recommended_Action: Supplemental irrigation where available; reduce weed competition
Prevention: Conserve moisture by deep ploughing after monsoon; drought-tolerant varieties; sow when soil has moisture (watar)
Applicable_District_Region: Rain-fed (barani): Attock, Chakwal, Jhelum, Rawalpindi, Khushab, Mianwali
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans; Barani Agricultural Research Institute, Chakwal

Symptoms: Crop falls flat after rain or wind, grain filling reduced
Relevant_Conditions: Excess nitrogen, heavy irrigation before storms, tall varieties
Recommended_Action: Avoid irrigation when strong wind is forecast
Prevention: Balanced N; lodging-resistant varieties; follow PMD forecasts for irrigation scheduling
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Pakistan Meteorological Department - agromet advisories

Symptoms: Poor and uneven germination, thin stand
Possible_Cause: Late sowing, poor seedbed, untreated or low-quality seed
Relevant_Conditions: Late rice/cotton harvest delaying land preparation
Recommended_Action: Increase seed rate by 10-25% for late sowing
Prevention: Use certified treated seed; sow Nov 1-20 in irrigated areas, Oct 15-Nov 15 in barani; drill sowing
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans

Symptoms: Water-soaked streaks on leaf edges turning yellow-white; leaves dry from tip (kresek in seedlings)
Possible_Cause: Bacterial leaf blight - Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae
Relevant_Conditions: Heavy rain, flooding, strong winds, high nitrogen; Basmati varieties susceptible
Recommended_Action: Drain field temporarily; avoid extra nitrogen; copper-based sprays may limit spread
Prevention: Resistant varieties; balanced NPK; avoid clipping seedling tips; remove infected stubble
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (AARI); IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: Spindle-shaped grey-centred lesions with brown margins on leaves; neck turns black and breaks
Relevant_Conditions: Cool nights, high humidity, prolonged leaf wetness, excess nitrogen
Recommended_Action: Spray recommended fungicide (e.g. tricyclazole) at boot stage and at 50% heading
Prevention: Resistant varieties; split N application; seed treatment
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (AARI); IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: Spikelets give white chalky or brown discoloured grain; grain spots
Possible_Cause: Grain discoloration / brown spot - Bipolaris oryzae and others
Relevant_Conditions: Humid weather at flowering, nutrient-poor soils
Recommended_Action: Fungicide spray at heading where history of disease
Prevention: Balanced fertilizer incl. potassium; seed treatment; clean seed
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: Tall, thin, pale seedlings that later die; white fungal growth at base
Relevant_Conditions: Infected seed; warm nursery conditions
Recommended_Action: Remove and destroy affected seedlings
Prevention: Seed treatment with recommended fungicide; salt-water seed selection
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (AARI)

Symptoms: Central shoot dries (dead heart); at heading white empty panicles (white heads)
Possible_Cause: Rice stem borers - yellow stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas)
Relevant_Conditions: Warm humid monsoon; continuous rice cropping; stubble left in field
Recommended_Action: Apply recommended granular insecticide in standing water when damage exceeds 5% dead hearts
Prevention: Destroy stubble after harvest; light traps; transplant on time; pheromone traps for monitoring
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (AARI); Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories

Symptoms: Leaves folded lengthwise with white streaks where green tissue is scraped
Relevant_Conditions: Shaded humid fields, high nitrogen
Recommended_Action: Insecticide spray if more than 2 freshly damaged leaves per hill
Prevention: Balanced nitrogen; conserve spiders and parasitoids
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: Circular patches of yellowing and drying plants (hopper burn); insects at plant base
Relevant_Conditions: Dense planting, excess nitrogen, continuous flooding, overuse of pyrethroids
Recommended_Action: Drain field for 3-4 days; spray selective insecticide directed at plant base
Prevention: Avoid excess N; alternate wetting and drying; avoid early broad-spectrum sprays
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank; Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (AARI)

Symptoms: Patches of stunted plants with brown rusty spots on older leaves 2-4 weeks after transplanting (khaira)
Relevant_Conditions: Waterlogged calcareous soils, high pH, high bicarbonate water
Recommended_Action: Apply zinc sulphate to soil or spray 0.5% zinc sulphate
Prevention: Apply zinc sulphate at transplanting on deficient fields
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept); Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (AARI)

Symptoms: Empty or partially filled grains (high sterility)
Relevant_Conditions: Temperatures above 35 C during flowering (late July-Aug for early transplanting)
Recommended_Action: Maintain standing water to cool canopy
Prevention: Transplant Basmati after mid-July so flowering falls in cooler weather; heat-tolerant varieties
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (AARI); Pakistan Meteorological Department - agromet advisories

Symptoms: Yellowish, weak, overaged seedlings; poor establishment
Possible_Cause: Poor nursery management or transplanting seedlings older than 35-40 days
Relevant_Conditions: Delayed transplanting due to canal water shortage
Recommended_Action: Transplant 25-35 day-old seedlings; 2 seedlings per hill at recommended spacing
Prevention: Plan nursery sowing dates by variety (Basmati: nursery June 1-20)
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (AARI)

Symptoms: High water use, falling water table, rising pumping costs
Possible_Cause: Continuous flooding in puddled transplanted rice
Relevant_Conditions: Tubewell-dependent rice areas with declining groundwater
Recommended_Action: Adopt alternate wetting and drying (AWD) after establishment
Prevention: Direct seeded rice (DSR) or AWD; laser land levelling
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank; Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC)

Symptoms: Leaves curl downwards, yellow and sticky; sooty mould; reduced vigour
Possible_Cause: Whitefly - Bemisia tabaci (also spreads cotton leaf curl virus)
Relevant_Conditions: Hot dry weather (Jul-Sep), overuse of broad-spectrum insecticides, nearby host crops
Recommended_Action: Spray recommended selective insecticide when above economic threshold (approx 5 adults/leaf); rotate chemical groups
Prevention: Sow on recommended dates; remove weed hosts; conserve natural enemies; avoid early pyrethroids
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan; Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories

Symptoms: Upward/downward leaf curling, thickened veins, leaf-like outgrowths (enations) under leaves; stunted plants
Possible_Cause: Cotton leaf curl virus (CLCuV), spread by whitefly
Relevant_Conditions: Early infection (first 60 days) with high whitefly populations; susceptible varieties
Recommended_Action: Uproot heavily infected early plants; control whitefly vector
Prevention: Grow CLCuV-tolerant approved varieties; manage whitefly; avoid very early sowing; remove ratoon cotton & weed hosts
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan; Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC)

Symptoms: Rosette flowers (petals webbed together); pink larvae inside bolls; seeds damaged; lint stained
Relevant_Conditions: Carry-over from stored seed and sticks; late-season crop; Bt resistance
Recommended_Action: Pheromone-based mating disruption; recommended spray at threshold; destroy rosette flowers
Prevention: Destroy cotton sticks/residue; fumigate seed; avoid late irrigation; PB-rope technology
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan; Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories

Symptoms: Holes in squares and bolls with frass; shed fruiting parts
Relevant_Conditions: Warm humid conditions; non-Bt or low-expression varieties
Recommended_Action: Spray recommended insecticide at threshold; hand-pick larvae on small farms
Prevention: Bt varieties with refuge; light & pheromone traps; intercropping trap crops
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan

Symptoms: Leaves curl upward, edges turn yellow then reddish-brown (hopper burn)
Relevant_Conditions: Hot humid weather early season
Recommended_Action: Spray recommended insecticide when 1-2 nymphs/adults per leaf
Prevention: Seed treatment with systemic insecticide; tolerant hairy-leaf varieties
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan

Symptoms: Silvery scratches on leaves, leaves cupped upward
Relevant_Conditions: Hot dry weather in May-June
Recommended_Action: Spray if 8-10 thrips per leaf
Prevention: Seed treatment; avoid water stress early
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan

Symptoms: White cottony masses on stems and leaves, plants stunted, sooty mould
Relevant_Conditions: Hot dry conditions, infested weeds and field borders
Recommended_Action: Spot-spray infested plants and borders with recommended insecticide
Prevention: Clean field borders; destroy infested weeds; monitor early
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan; CABI Plantwise Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: Shedding of flowers and young bolls; poor boll retention
Possible_Cause: Heat stress (above 40-45 C) with low humidity
Relevant_Conditions: May-July heatwaves in southern Punjab
Recommended_Action: Irrigate at shorter intervals during heatwave (evening irrigation)
Prevention: Sow in recommended window (April-May); heat-tolerant varieties; potassium nutrition
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan; Pakistan Meteorological Department - agromet advisories

Symptoms: Yellowing between veins of older leaves, edges turn brown; small bolls
Relevant_Conditions: Light-textured soils, intensive cropping without K
Recommended_Action: Foliar spray of potassium nitrate or potassium sulphate
Prevention: Apply potassium based on soil test
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept)

Symptoms: Shedding of squares, deformed bolls, cracked petioles
Relevant_Conditions: Calcareous alkaline soils, drought
Recommended_Action: Foliar boron spray (borax/boric acid) at squaring and flowering
Prevention: Soil-test-based boron application
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept)

Symptoms: Gappy stand and seedling mortality
Possible_Cause: Poor seed quality, crust formation, salinity
Relevant_Conditions: Saline-sodic patches, heavy irrigation after sowing
Recommended_Action: Re-sow gaps within 2 weeks; light irrigation to soften crust
Prevention: Delinted treated seed; bed-furrow planting; gypsum on sodic patches
Applicable_District_Region: Cotton belt: Multan, Khanewal, Vehari, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah
Source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan

Symptoms: Leaves yellow and dry; split cane shows red tissue with white cross bands and sour smell
Relevant_Conditions: Waterlogging, monsoon humidity, susceptible varieties
Recommended_Action: Uproot and burn affected clumps; do not ratoon infected fields
Prevention: Use disease-free setts from healthy nursery; resistant varieties; crop rotation
Applicable_District_Region: Sugarcane areas: Faisalabad, Jhang, Sargodha, Toba Tek Singh, Chiniot, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur, Mandi Bahauddin, Layyah
Source: Sugarcane Research Institute, Faisalabad (AARI); CABI Plantwise Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: Black whip-like structure emerging from top of cane; thin grassy shoots
Relevant_Conditions: Ratoon crops, dry hot weather
Recommended_Action: Rogue and destroy smut whips in a bag before spores disperse
Prevention: Hot water treatment of setts; resistant varieties; limit ratoons
Applicable_District_Region: Sugarcane areas: Faisalabad, Jhang, Sargodha, Toba Tek Singh, Chiniot, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur, Mandi Bahauddin, Layyah
Source: Sugarcane Research Institute, Faisalabad (AARI)

Symptoms: Dead hearts in young shoots; bore holes in internodes
Possible_Cause: Stem borers (early shoot borer, top borer, stalk borer)
Relevant_Conditions: Hot dry pre-monsoon (top borer: whitish midrib streaks)
Recommended_Action: Release Trichogramma cards; apply recommended granular insecticide at tillering
Prevention: Remove dead hearts; trash management; light traps; resistant varieties
Applicable_District_Region: Sugarcane areas: Faisalabad, Jhang, Sargodha, Toba Tek Singh, Chiniot, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur, Mandi Bahauddin, Layyah
Source: Sugarcane Research Institute, Faisalabad (AARI); Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories

Symptoms: White fluffy insects on leaf undersides; sooty mould
Relevant_Conditions: Humid monsoon period, dense crop
Recommended_Action: Release biocontrol agents (e.g. Epiricania for pyrilla); spray only if severe
Prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen; conserve natural enemies
Applicable_District_Region: Sugarcane areas: Faisalabad, Jhang, Sargodha, Toba Tek Singh, Chiniot, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur, Mandi Bahauddin, Layyah
Source: Sugarcane Research Institute, Faisalabad (AARI)

Symptoms: Weeds covering inter-rows; poor tiller count
Relevant_Conditions: Wide row spacing and frequent irrigation
Recommended_Action: Inter-row hoeing; recommended pre/post emergence herbicide
Prevention: Trench planting; trash mulching; intercropping in autumn cane
Applicable_District_Region: Sugarcane areas: Faisalabad, Jhang, Sargodha, Toba Tek Singh, Chiniot, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur, Mandi Bahauddin, Layyah
Source: Sugarcane Research Institute, Faisalabad (AARI)

Symptoms: Poor germination of setts; gaps
Possible_Cause: Old/dry setts, wrong depth, low soil moisture
Relevant_Conditions: Planting during extreme heat or cold
Recommended_Action: Gap filling with pre-germinated setts
Prevention: Plant autumn (Sep-Oct) or spring (Feb-Mar) with fresh 3-bud setts treated with fungicide
Applicable_District_Region: Sugarcane areas: Faisalabad, Jhang, Sargodha, Toba Tek Singh, Chiniot, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur, Mandi Bahauddin, Layyah
Source: Sugarcane Research Institute, Faisalabad (AARI)

Symptoms: Ragged holes in whorl leaves, sawdust-like frass in funnel; larvae with inverted Y on head
Relevant_Conditions: Warm weather, spring and autumn maize; invasive pest since 2019
Recommended_Action: Spray recommended insecticide into whorl when 10-20% plants infested; early morning/evening
Prevention: Early detection scouting; pheromone traps; timely sowing; conserve natural enemies
Applicable_District_Region: Maize areas: Okara, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Kasur, Faisalabad, Vehari, Sheikhupura
Source: FAO - Plant Production and Protection; Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories; CIMMYT Wheat & Maize Doctor

Symptoms: Shot holes in leaves in a row, dead heart; tunnelling in stem
Relevant_Conditions: Hot humid summer, autumn maize
Recommended_Action: Apply recommended granular insecticide in whorl
Prevention: Destroy stubble; timely sowing; Trichogramma release
Applicable_District_Region: Maize areas: Okara, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Kasur, Faisalabad, Vehari, Sheikhupura
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans

Symptoms: Long elliptical grey-green to tan lesions on leaves
Relevant_Conditions: Moderate temperature with high humidity and dew
Recommended_Action: Fungicide spray at early disease onset in seed crops
Prevention: Resistant hybrids; crop rotation; residue management
Applicable_District_Region: Maize areas: Okara, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Kasur, Faisalabad, Vehari, Sheikhupura
Source: CIMMYT Wheat & Maize Doctor

Symptoms: Delayed silking, poor pollination, gaps of missing grains on cob
Possible_Cause: Heat and drought stress at flowering
Relevant_Conditions: Spring maize flowering in May-June heat above 38 C
Recommended_Action: Irrigate frequently around flowering
Prevention: Sow spring maize late Jan-Feb; heat-tolerant hybrids
Applicable_District_Region: Maize areas: Okara, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Kasur, Faisalabad, Vehari, Sheikhupura
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans; Maize & Millets Research Institute, Sahiwal

Symptoms: Yellow V-shaped area starting at leaf tip on lower leaves
Relevant_Conditions: Heavy rain leaching, sandy soils, insufficient top-dressing
Recommended_Action: Top-dress urea at knee-high and tasseling
Prevention: Split N applications; soil testing
Applicable_District_Region: Maize areas: Okara, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Kasur, Faisalabad, Vehari, Sheikhupura
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept)

Symptoms: Broad white/yellow bands either side of midrib on young leaves
Relevant_Conditions: Calcareous soils, high pH, cold soils
Recommended_Action: Foliar spray of 0.5% zinc sulphate
Prevention: Basal zinc sulphate application
Applicable_District_Region: Maize areas: Okara, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Kasur, Faisalabad, Vehari, Sheikhupura
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept)

Recommended_Action: Harvest at doka stage and cure artificially
Prevention: Bag bunches; early varieties that ripen before monsoon
Applicable_District_Region: Main growing districts (by area, 2014-25 in source data): Muzaffargarh, Bhakkar, Jhang, Bahawalpur, Layyah, Multan
Source: Date Palm Research Station, Jhang (AARI)

Symptoms: Yellow vein patterns, leaf distortion, twig dieback
Relevant_Conditions: Aphid and psyllid vectors
Recommended_Action: Remove infected trees; vector control
Prevention: Certified nursery plants
Applicable_District_Region: Main growing districts (by area, 2014-25 in source data): Rahim Yar Khan, Nankana Sahib, Sheikhupura, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Sargodha
Source: Horticultural Research Institute / Citrus Research Institute Sargodha (AARI)

Symptoms: Fruit splitting / cracking
Relevant_Conditions: Heavy irrigation after dry spell
Recommended_Action: Regular irrigation
Prevention: Boron foliar spray; mulching
Applicable_District_Region: Main growing districts (by area, 2014-25 in source data): Muzaffargarh, Multan, Rahim Yar Khan, Sahiwal, Lodhran, Okara
Source: Horticultural Research Institute / Citrus Research Institute Sargodha (AARI)

Symptoms: Low yield, weak shoots
Relevant_Conditions: Bushes left unpruned in dormant season
Recommended_Action: Prune heavily in Dec-Jan to 1-1.5 m
Prevention: Annual pruning; manure application
Applicable_District_Region: Main growing districts (by area, 2014-25 in source data): Multan, Vehari, Lodhran, Muzaffargarh, Bahawalpur, Kasur
Source: Horticultural Research Institute / Citrus Research Institute Sargodha (AARI)

Symptoms: Maggots in ripening ber fruit
Relevant_Conditions: Fruit maturity Feb-April
Recommended_Action: Collect fallen fruit; bait spray
Prevention: Orchard sanitation; summer ploughing
Applicable_District_Region: Main growing districts (by area, 2014-25 in source data): Bahawalpur, Multan, Kasur, Rahim Yar Khan, Bhakkar, Sargodha
Source: Horticultural Research Institute / Citrus Research Institute Sargodha (AARI)

Symptoms: White crust on soil surface, patchy growth, leaf tip burn
Relevant_Conditions: Poor drainage, saline tubewell water, high evaporation
Recommended_Action: Leach salts with good-quality canal water; grow salt-tolerant crops (barley, cotton, sugar beet)
Prevention: Laser land levelling; drainage; avoid brackish water; organic matter
Applicable_District_Region: Saline patches: Faisalabad, Jhang, Sheikhupura, Hafizabad, Toba Tek Singh, Bahawalnagar
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept); Soil Salinity Research Institute, Pindi Bhattian

Symptoms: Hard, dark, poorly drained soil; water stands on surface; very poor germination
Relevant_Conditions: Use of sodic tubewell water (high RSC)
Recommended_Action: Apply gypsum based on soil/water test; incorporate and leach
Prevention: Gypsum with irrigation; green manuring; avoid high-RSC water
Applicable_District_Region: Central Punjab: Faisalabad, Hafizabad, Sheikhupura, Gujranwala, Kasur
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept)

Symptoms: Crops submerged, yellowing, root rot after heavy rain or river flooding
Relevant_Conditions: Monsoon floods along Indus, Chenab, Jhelum, Ravi, Sutlej; hill torrents in DG Khan/Rajanpur
Recommended_Action: Drain fields quickly; top-dress N once soil dries; re-sow short-duration crops
Prevention: Follow PMD/PDMA flood forecasts; raised beds; flood-tolerant varieties
Applicable_District_Region: Riverine areas: Rajanpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Muzaffargarh, Rahim Yar Khan, Jhang, Layyah
Source: Pakistan Meteorological Department - agromet advisories; PDMA Punjab

Symptoms: Wilting, leaf scorch, reduced growth during heatwave
Relevant_Conditions: May-June in southern Punjab
Recommended_Action: Irrigate in evening; avoid spraying in heat
Prevention: Heat-tolerant varieties; adjust sowing dates; mulching
Applicable_District_Region: Southern Punjab: Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Multan, Dera Ghazi Khan, Bahawalnagar
Source: Pakistan Meteorological Department - agromet advisories

Symptoms: Crusting and moisture stress in sandy soils; low yields
Possible_Cause: Low water-holding capacity of sandy Thal soils
Relevant_Conditions: Low rainfall, wind erosion
Recommended_Action: Light frequent irrigation; sprinkler/drip where available
Prevention: Windbreaks; organic matter; drought-tolerant crops (gram, guar, bajra)
Applicable_District_Region: Thal & rain-fed (barani): Bhakkar, Layyah, Khushab, Mianwali, Jhang, Chakwal, Attock
Source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad - crop production plans; Arid Zone Research Institute, Bhakkar

Symptoms: General poor growth despite NPK use
Possible_Cause: Low soil organic matter (below 1% common in Punjab)
Relevant_Conditions: Residue burning, no manure, intensive cropping
Recommended_Action: Apply farmyard manure or compost
Prevention: Stop residue burning; green manuring (sesbania); crop rotation with legumes
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Soil Fertility Research Institute, Lahore (Punjab Agriculture Dept)

Symptoms: Smoke and smog, loss of soil organic matter
Possible_Cause: Burning of rice straw / crop residues
Relevant_Conditions: Short window between rice harvest and wheat sowing
Recommended_Action: Use happy seeder / super seeder to sow wheat into residue
Prevention: Residue incorporation; baling straw for fodder/energy; follow Punjab smog regulations
Applicable_District_Region: Rice belt: Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Gujrat
Source: Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories; Environment Protection Department Punjab

Symptoms: Pest outbreaks after repeated spraying; insecticides stop working
Possible_Cause: Insecticide resistance and destruction of natural enemies
Relevant_Conditions: Overuse and wrong mixtures of pesticides
Recommended_Action: Spray only at economic threshold; rotate modes of action
Prevention: Integrated Pest Management (IPM): scouting, traps, biocontrol, resistant varieties
Applicable_District_Region: All Punjab
Source: Punjab Agriculture Department (Extension Wing) - seasonal crop advisories; FAO - Plant Production and Protection

Symptoms: Swarms of insects eating all green parts
Relevant_Conditions: Breeding after unusual rains in desert areas (Cholistan, Thal)
Recommended_Action: Report immediately to Plant Protection Department; coordinated control
Prevention: Monitoring through FAO Locust Watch & Department of Plant Protection advisories
Applicable_District_Region: Desert border areas: Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalnagar, Bhakkar, Layyah
Source: FAO - Plant Production and Protection (Locust Watch); Department of Plant Protection, Pakistan
